historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Revenue 5yr CAGR (6.7%) diverges >30% from equity 5yr CAGR (3.5%) only because FY2020 is a COVID trough base; FY2018-FY2025 revenue is flat (1,588.6 -> 1,570.2). EPS 5yr CAGR is meaningless off FY2020 EPS of US$0.002.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = FCF - SBC - interest income: FY2020 120.4, FY2022 187.3, FY2025 94.4. Owner-FCF CAGRs track reported closely (SBC is immaterial); the decline is the capex step-up (US$45m FY2022 -> US$87m FY2025 -> ~US$115m FY2026E) for three new factories, plus FY2025 margin compression. Payout >100% of FCF in FY2025 (dividends 169.2 vs FCF 107.4) funded from the net-cash pile.

scenario_narratives.base: 2026 is the trough investment year management says it is: revenue +1.5% on flat shipments, EBITDA margin ~12% as Indonesia/Vietnam/Bangladesh II ramp, the Philippines winds down and handbags lose money. The new capacity fills over 2027-28 with Sports customers diversifying away from China, revenue growing 6-7% and margin recovering to the FY2023-25 average of ~14%, a ~5% PAT CAGR -- short of the high-single-digit plan target because the last two ramps (Indonesia, Philippines) both ran over cost. Thereafter a mature, low-growth OEM.
scenario_narratives.bull: Supply-chain diversification and vendor consolidation favour multi-country premium ODMs: the three new factories ramp cleanly, new Sports and Fashion customers fill them, Luxury/Fashion demand recovers, and the handbag business becomes a second leg. Revenue compounds ~9-10% in 2027-28 and margins regain the FY2024 peak (~15.5%), delivering the plan's high-single-digit-plus PAT CAGR.
scenario_narratives.bear: The ramp repeats the Indonesia/Philippines pattern and coincides with demand weakness: the dominant Sports customer (Nike) shifts mix or volume away, US tariffs force further 'tariff support' concessions, and Luxury/Fashion keeps declining. Revenue slips in 2027 and margin settles at ~12% (below the FY2025 13.1%), with the new capacity under-utilised and the 70% payout plus special dividends draining the remaining net cash.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A mature, cash-rich footwear contract manufacturer with flat revenue over 2018-25 is worth its normalised owner FCF capitalised at a modest multiple plus its net cash. The value question is whether the 2026-28 capacity build earns its cost of capital: the base case assumes margins return to the FY2023-25 average, not the FY2024 peak, and the terminal multiple is capped at 12x for a cyclical, customer-concentrated OEM.
key_risks_to_valuation: Customer concentration: mix or volume shifts at the largest Sports customer already drove the FY2025-H1 2026 PRC-factory deleverage
Ramp execution at three new factories simultaneously, after the Indonesia/Philippines overruns
US tariff policy and continued 'tariff support' concessions to customers
Net cash is being distributed (70% payout + US$60m/yr special returns through 2026) faster than FCF replenishes it; the excess-return programme ends in 2026
Seasonal working-capital swing makes the June balance sheet understate through-year net cash by ~US$100m; the bridge normalises it

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 844.01m ordinary shares in issue at 30-Jun-2026 (H1 FY2026 interim note, incl. the share-award trust pool) + all 18.85m outstanding 2017-Scheme options, every tranche in the money (strikes HK$7.65-9.46 vs HK$13.11); exercise proceeds US$21.4m added in the equity bridge. Held FLAT thereafter because SBC is expensed in the flows. Options have been the real dilution channel (15.1m exercised in FY2025, ~1.8%); no buybacks executed FY2022-H1 2026 -- the Excess Cash Return Programme has been paid entirely as special dividends, so the flat count is a modelling convention the company is not funding with repurchases.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share option expense' US$278k (note 31); no equity-award tax withholding (HK option scheme, gross settlement). FY2021-24 expense ran US$1.5-5.8m; forward path set at 0.25% of revenue (multi-year average, and the accounting charge understates the economic cost of options granted well below market).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in USD (Group functional and presentation currency, read off the FY2025 AR and H1 FY2026 interim); price quoted in HKD on HKEX. Per-share values computed in USD and converted at USD/HKD 7.8476 (Yahoo HKD=X, regularMarketTime 2026-10-16). Parity check: HKD is pegged in the 7.75-7.85 band, rate sits inside it; no USD dual listing exists to cross-check. Direction: USD x 7.8476 = HKD.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, so a USD build: US 10y ~4.3% + beta ~1.0 x 5.5% ERP = ~9.8%, rounded to 10.0%. Net cash, so WACC = cost of equity. Customer concentration, tariff and ramp-execution risk are charged in the bear scenario and its 25% weight, not as a WACC premium; WACC identical across scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt: lease liabilities US$8.43m (3.04 current + 5.39 non-current, 30-Jun-2026) included in total_debt; lease principal (~US$3.3m/yr) NOT deducted from flows; right-of-use depreciation (~US$6.7m) stays inside the D&A % and the capex-like renewal is in the capex %. Immaterial either way (<1% of EV).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI deducted once in the equity bridge at book (US$13.5m, 30-Jun-2026). NCI profit share is ~US$1m/yr (<1% of net profit). FY0 check: EBIT 149.3 x (1-16% book rate) + after-tax interest ~10.7 = ~136 vs attributable net profit 138.0.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF + non-US/cyclical adaptations (dcf-methods routing row 2: non-US operating company, cyclical footwear OEM/ODM; USD filer with HKD quote). First valuation of this ticker -- no MEMORY.md entry, no prior DCF. Owner FCF FY2025 = reported FCF 107.4 (OCF 194.7 - PPE capex 87.3) - SBC 0.3 - interest income 12.7 = 94.4; interest income stripped because net cash (US$367m at Dec-25) is ~4x the FCF base. ANCHOR CONSTRUCTION: balance sheet is the latest filing (30-Jun-2026), but June is this company's seasonal working-capital trough (H1 WC outflow 138.7m in 2026, 106.3m in 2025, while full-year WC was ~flat in FY2025 and +36m in FY2024). Year 1 of the projection is full calendar FY2026, so the H1-2026 operating and capex outflow already in the June balance (OCF -48.4, PPE -63.1, deposits -0.5 = 112.0) is added back in the bridge to avoid charging it twice; the HK42c interim dividend paid 18-Sep-2026 (US$45.2m, price is ex) is deducted. Equivalent to Dec-25 net cash rolled forward for distributions, option proceeds and the H1 subsidiary disposal. SBC is not zero but tiny (house and street within ~1%). Guidance: FY2026 shipments broadly flat, 2026 an 'investment year'; Three-Year Plan 2026-28 targets high-single-digit PAT CAGR with ~20m pairs of new capacity (Indonesia x2, Vietnam, Bangladesh II) against 55.0m pairs shipped in FY2025; Philippines phased shutdown from July 2026; handbag business loss-making in 2026.

base.growth_rates_rationale: FY2026 +1.5% = H1 run-rate (+1.5%) with shipments guided broadly flat; 2027-28 +6-7% as the ~20m pairs of new capacity (+36% on 55m pairs shipped) ramps net of the Philippines closure -- below full capacity utilisation given the ramp track record; fades to 2% terminal for a business whose revenue was flat 2018-2025.
base.ebitda_margin_path_rationale: FY2026 12.0% = H1 FY2026 underlying (104.4 EBITDA less 8.9 disposal gain = 12.1%) with H2 Philippines exit costs; recovers to 14.0-14.3% by 2028, the FY2023-25 average (13.9/15.4/13.1), i.e. new factories reach FY2023-25 efficiency but not the FY2024 peak. Implies ~5% PAT CAGR 2025-28, below management's high-single-digit target.
base.capex_pct_path_rationale: FY2026 ~US$115m (H1 63.6m, of which 35.4m new factories); normalises toward 4%, above the 3.0-3.6% of FY2018-24 because the footprint is larger.
base.cash_tax_rate_path_rationale: Cash taxes paid have run 5-8% of EBIT (FY2025 10.1m on EBIT ~149m) vs a 15-16% book rate; ramps to 15% by 2029 as Pillar Two minimum tax (Vietnam QDMTT, in force from 2024) and lapsing new-factory incentives catch up.
base.wc_capture_pct_rationale: Contract manufacturer: receivables + inventory exceed payables, so growth consumes cash (negative capture).

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a single dominant customer, three simultaneous factory ramps after two that ran over cost, and an explicit unresolved US-tariff headwind. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs clean execution, customer wins and a Luxury/Fashion recovery all at once. Base 50%: guided trough year followed by partial margin recovery, consistent with management's plan discounted for track record.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
